newsitem.title: UK: BA to cut 400 cargo jobs at Heathrow airport.
newsitem.headline: BA to cut 400 cargo jobs at Heathrow airport.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Thursday that its World Cargo division plans to cut 400 jobs over the next two years from a current workforce of 1,500 at London Heathrow as a result of increased automation.
The company said in a statement that it wants to make the cuts by voluntary severance, redeployment or early retirement of staff and hoped to avoid any compulsory redundancies.

BA is spending 150 million pounds on a new cargo centre, which it says will double handling capacity at Heathrow to 800,000 tonnes of cargo a year when it opens in early 1999 but will also bring a big increase in automation.

"While the opening of our new World Cargocentre and our investment in modern technology will improve our customer service and overall efficiency it will, regrettably, mean the business needs fewer people in future," said chief executive Robert Ayling.

BA said the announcement marked the mid-way point in a four-year overhaul of World Cargo, where last year sales were up nine percent at 563 million pounds, out of total group turnover of 7.76 billion pounds.

BA sent a letter to all its British-based cargo staff in July last year seeking their views on early retirement, voluntary severance or part-time working. The airline said the decision to cut 400 jobs was to be confirmed to staff and their unions through a series of briefings starting today.
A spokesman said the cargo business currently employs 2,800 people and the latest job cuts were part of BA's wider rationalisation programme announced last year.

Under its business efficiency programme, the airline aims to shed 5,000 of 49,000 existing staff in Britain to make way for new recruits and help cut a billion pounds off annual costs before the end of the decade.
